gryphaea.supports: The named Jurassic Gryphaea dilatata teaching specimen has two articulated unequal valves: a flat upper right valve and curved lower left valve, with umbo and growth lines. The candidate is shell-only; no living animal or exact specimen claim.

folded-strata-outcrop.supports: NPS describes folding and alternating anticlines/synclines. Candidate is an original teaching section with no named locality or strain claim.

volcanic-bomb.supports: NPS describes a spindle lava bomb as a rounded liquid blob with a stretched end and degassing cracks. Candidate is an original stylized spindle clast, not that specimen; its shallow relief remains artistic.

teredolites-wood-boring-cast.supports: PRI Digital Atlas describes Teredolites borings in fossil wood and identifies a Paleocene specimen; it does not identify a producer or tree species.

The specialist KU Ichnology description gives clavate/club-shaped to flask-shaped tubes in woodgrounds, tapering from chamber to aperture, and notes orientation relative to wood grain. It cites Kelly and Bromley 1984.

third_party_assets: No external media, models, textures or scanned geometry are incorporated; references remain consulted-only and their pages are not treated as asset licenses.
